headline: Binder and ligand generators move toward multi-objective, multi-variant design targets
label: Computational Antibody And Binder Design
summary: New generative models optimize paratopes across antigen variants, model all-atom contacts, and enforce cross-component constraints in conjugates and pockets.
synthesis: The dominant thread is generative design conditioned on more than a single affinity score against a single fixed target. Germinal Multi optimizes one paratope jointly across multiple antigen variants, reporting designs that bind EGFR variants and neutralize SARS-CoV-2; an antigen-specific protein language model guides CDR optimization for antigen recognition. PDZ-binding motifs are designed by moving along directions in a shared PDZ-PBM latent space learned from affinity prediction, supporting single-target design. Pallatom2 extends this to all-atom joint modeling of sequence, backbone, side chains and target contacts in a 65.9M-parameter model with reported experimental validation. On the small-molecule side, PFM uses a perturbed conditional probability path for pocket-conditioned 3D generation (Vina -7.12), and CupOFMoCA enforces cross-component chemical constraints for PROTAC and peptide-drug conjugate assembly. Pyrite adds evaluation infrastructure: 1,500 protein-ligand pairs for ranking cofolded poses, with LLM agents reaching 74% accuracy. Modalities and evidence standards differ, precluding cross-method comparison.
